writer.name: Claude Opus 5.5, the hypnosis guide lane's writer (the splices and their fixes; the words are Emulate's)

findings.label: B7 short landing at paragraph end
examples: Try "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening."
findings.reason: It ends the paragraph as the old line did ("“Tell me what you remember, I’m listening.” works well here."): a line for the reader to say to the part, not a summing-up.

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is Emulate's rewrite of the words it replaces (SOURCE.txt), so it follows their points in order by design; the turns are Emulate's own ("in the past", "this part knows it", "Try").

findings.label: E36/E41 heavy second person
findings.reason: The guide speaks to the reader as "you" throughout; here "you" is the reader who may have fooled himself, and the line he can say to the part.
